question.problem:
The projection of the intersection between the elliptic paraboloid $4(x-5)^{2}+6(y+4)^{2}=z+8$ and the plane 
$z=4$  onto the $xy$-plane is an ellipse. What are the lengths of the semi-axes of the ellipse?
question.worked_solution:
To find the intersection of the paraboloid and the plane $z=4$, we substitute $z=4$ into the equation of the paraboloid, and simplify:

$$
\begin{aligned}4(x-5)^{2}+6(y+4)^{2}=z+8 \\ 4(x-5)^{2}+6(y+4)^{2}=4+8 \\ 4(x-5)^{2}+6(y+4)^{2}=12 \\ \frac{(x-5)^{2}}{3}+\frac{(y+4)^{2}}{2} & =1 \\ \frac{(x-5)^{2}}{(\sqrt{3})^{2}}+\frac{(y+4)^{2}}{(\sqrt{2})^{2}} & =1\end{aligned}
$$

This gives us the equation of an ellipse with semi-axes of lengths $\sqrt{3}$ and $\sqrt{2}.$
